gap: Because no autonomous runtime-repair capability exists, the second permitted path ('a pre-approved runtime action whose event is durably audited') has nothing to be durably audited — there is no event-audit mechanism for runtime actions at all. The requirement is satisfied only by omission (nothing autonomous can act outside git yet), not by a positive control that would catch one if it existed. The cited positive control is narrower than it reads: guard-dangerous-command.py refuses destructive commands (force push, recursive delete, teardown, `terraform apply -auto-approve`, `gcloud ... delete`, `kubectl delete`, destructive SQL) but not non-destructive production mutations made outside git, such as `gcloud run deploy`, `gcloud run services update`, `kubectl apply`/`edit` or a plain `terraform apply`, so an agent can still make an invisible change. Nothing configures Cloud Audit Logs in Terraform (no google_project_iam_audit_config), and Argo CD's selfHeal on dev, which would revert out-of-git edits to reconciled objects, runs on the suspended control plane (ADR 0093).

current: A Rust-native model and policy release path exists for the forms the platform trains (ADR 0083). Models: the deep brain fits and distils a candidate, scores it on its own held-out tail and against the incumbent, and promotes it through Platform::promote_model. The kernel journals a ModelPromotion before the registry adopts it (qip-kernel/src/model_serving.rs). ModelRegistry::promote_artifact verifies the artifact's SHA-256 digest and refuses new bytes under an old version (qip-ai/src/registry.rs:304-343). The composition root writes the digest-named artifact to its storage (qip-deepbrain/src/main.rs:637, :865); qip-storage has a GCS backend. The registry has a ModelStage::Shadow stage. Cells receive the promoted set through the policy payload's `trained_models` ModelManifest slot and refuse a plan whose inline model's digest the manifest does not name (Cell::check_models_promoted, qip-edge/src/cell.rs:2645). Policies: the policy payload is twelve typed slots under one HMAC signature and one sequence, applied by a cell as one fact, and a lower sequence is refused.
gap: What is missing: (1) a signed OCI manifest, since artifacts are digest-named JSON and the policy is HMAC-authenticated rather than KMS/asymmetrically signed (ADR 0043's named gap; the KMS route the images use is available); (2) the ordered shadow score -> paper/replay -> stage locally -> activate sequence. Shadow exists as a registry stage, but no promotion walks it, and replay scoring is a held-out tail, not a paper or replay run. (3) Atomic activation of a model epoch across every consumer. (4) Weights in GCS for a deployed deep brain, which depends on its storage configuration and on a runnable deployment. None of this needs a Python runtime: C5 covers only large-model training.

current: Retention exists, but rollback does not. ModelRegistry never removes a card: retire() marks it Retired, and promote() does not demote the previous Production card. promote_artifact refuses to put different bytes under an already-promoted version (qip-ai/src/registry.rs:304-343). The deep brain writes each promoted artifact under its digest and never deletes one (qip-deepbrain/src/main.rs:865), so the previous epoch's exact bytes stay addressable by digest. production_version() would fall back to the older Production card if the newer one were retired, but it has no production caller, and no operation re-activates a previous epoch for cells. The policy payload's sequence rule refuses a lower sequence, so a rollback must republish the old content under a new sequence.
